message.content: Let's reintroduce a notion of multiple agents. I want to try and parse codex sessions as well. The best way to do this would be to make an agnostic scraper that finds things like tool calls, user info, etc across multiple types of sesssion formats, instead of trying to match one particular one. Keep the claude parsing but add another parser that's more flexible. There are some sample sessions in the checkpoints in the ~/p/entire-graph directory, there are a bunch of codex sessions there

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

attachment.content:
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- claude-in-chrome: Automates your Chrome browser to interact with web pages - clicking elements, filling forms, capturing screenshots, reading console logs, and navigating sites. Opens pages in new tabs within your existing Chrome session. Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. Always invoke BEFORE attempting to use any mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

We're working in /Users/stephanostsoucas/p/gossamer-multi-agent, a Rust CLI (gossamer) that indexes AI coding sessions from git checkpoint branches (entireio's `entire/checkpoints/v1`). It currently has full support for parsing "Claude Code" format session JSONL, and we're adding support for a second agent format, "Codex" (OpenAI Codex CLI/Desktop sessions), plus a goal of a general "agnostic" fallback parser for future agent formats.

Known architecture (already explored, don't re-derive):
- `src/parsers/mod.rs` + `src/parsers/claude_code.rs`: parses `metadata.json` + `full.jsonl` (or just `full.jsonl` for "shadow" branches) into a `ParsedSession` struct (session_id, agent_name, created_at, updated_at, cwd, session_name, branch, name_is_explicit, tokens_used) for the `sessions` SQLite table. `dispatch_session`/`dispatch_shadow_session` currently unconditionally call the claude_code parser regardless of actual agent.
- `src/ingest/claude_code.rs`: separately parses the same Claude JSONL format into text chunks (per-turn) for the witchcraft semantic-search DB. This is completely independent of `src/parsers/` and also assumes Claude's JSONL shape (`{"type":"user"|"assistant", "message":{"role":..,"content":..}}`).
- `src/commands/index.rs` and `src/commands/refresh.rs` call `crate::parsers::dispatch_session` / `dispatch_shadow_session` to populate the `sessions` table, and separately `src/commands/index.rs::run()` calls `ingest::claude_code::ingest_claude_code(&mut wc_db)` to populate the search DB.
- Claude metadata.json checkpoint-level has an `"agent"` field ("Claude Code" or "Codex" seen in real sample data at ~/p/entire-graph's `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch). Codex's raw `full.jsonl` has a totally different shape: top-level `{"type":"response_item"|"event_msg"|"session_meta"|"turn_context"|..., "payload": {...}}`, with user text at `payload.type=="user_message"` -> `payload.message`, assistant text at `payload.type=="agent_message"` -> `payload.message`, tool calls at `payload.type in ("function_call","custom_tool_call")` (fields `name`, `input`/`arguments`, `call_id`), tool results at `payload.type in ("function_call_output","custom_tool_call_output")` (fields `call_id`, `output`). There is ALSO a separate, already-normalized `transcript.jsonl` file (referenced in metadata.json under `sessions[].compact_transcript`) with much simpler shape: each line `{"v":1,"agent":"codex","type":"user"|"assistant","ts":"...","content":[{"type":"text","text":"..."}, {"type":"tool_use","id":..,"name":..,"input":..,"result":..}]}` — but for Claude Code sessions this same `transcript.jsonl` file exists but is EMPTY (0 bytes / 0 lines), so it can't be relied on universally.

1. `src/commands/show.rs` — how does it render a session transcript? Does it assume Claude's JSONL shape (`type`, `message.role`, `message.content`)? Would it break/show garbage for Codex's raw `full.jsonl`? Does it reference `transcript.jsonl`/compact_transcript anywhere already?

3. `tests/integration_test.rs` — do any tests construct fake `metadata.json`/`full.jsonl` fixtures and assert on `ingest_claude_code`, `dispatch_session`, or agent-name behavior? List test names and what fixture shape they use, so we know what must keep passing.
4. `src/db.rs` — does the `sessions` table schema or any migration already have provisions for multiple agents (e.g. indices, checks)? Just confirm agent_name is a free-text column with no enum constraint.
5. Search the whole `src/` tree for any other place that hardcodes "Claude Code" as a literal string or assumes only one agent format (e.g. `entire-plugin.yml`, `README.md` mentions are not needed — just `src/`).

content.text:
Note: ReportFindings was the wrong tool for this (it's for code-review findings, not investigation reports) — ignore that empty call. Here is the actual investigation report:

## 1. `src/commands/show.rs` — transcript rendering

Fully hardcoded to Claude's JSONL shape. `parse()` (line 496) and its helpers `parse_user`/`parse_asst` (633-695) match on `v["type"] == "user"|"assistant"|"system"|"custom-title"` and read `v["message"]["content"]` as either a string or an array of `{"type":"text"|"tool_use"|"tool_result"}` blocks (539, 543, 636-663, 671-693). Tool names are resolved via a `tool_names` map built from `message.content[].type=="tool_use"` (497-510).

Given Codex's raw `full.jsonl` shape (`{"type":"response_item"|"event_msg"|..., "payload":{...}}`), every line would fail the `match v["type"].as_str()` arms (524-546, all `_ => {}`), so `parse()` would silently produce **zero cards** — `run_at` would print `"No messages found."` (145-148), not garbage, but effectively unusable for Codex sessions.

No reference to `transcript.jsonl`/`compact_transcript` anywhere in the file — only two unrelated comments mentioning "Claude Code transcript"/"local Claude transcript" (show.rs:444, 1420, 1458), referring to the local `~/.claude/projects/*.jsonl` file, not the checkpoint's `transcript.jsonl`.

## 2. `session_list.rs` / agent-aware logic

- `sanitize_one_line` (session_list.rs:73-89) collapses interior whitespace/newlines to a single space, purely a display-safety helper — not agent-specific.
- `augment_with_jsonls` (195-262) only scans `~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl` and hardcodes `agent_name: "Claude Code".to_string()` for any untracked session found there (line 254) — assumes every local JSONL is Claude.
- `src/commands/mod.rs:126-128`: `agent_color(_name: &str) -> u8 { 214 }` — the name parameter is **ignored**; every agent renders the same orange. No per-agent icon/branching logic exists anywhere else; `author_color` (134-144) is per-human, unrelated.
- `src/commands/sessions.rs:86` just passes through `s.agent_name` into JSON output, no branching.
- `src/entity/session.rs:5` — `agent_name: String` field, no enum.
- `src/commands/session_start.rs:31` hardcodes `'Claude Code'` literally into the `INSERT` SQL for the SessionStart-hook-created row.

## 3. `tests/integration_test.rs` fixtures

- `create_checkpoint_branch()` (580-619) builds a synthetic checkpoint branch tree (`sessions/<id>/1/{metadata.json,full.jsonl}`) with `metadata.json = {"session_id","agent":"claude-code","created_at","summary":{"intent"}}` (note: lowercase `"claude-code"`, passed through as-is into `agent_name` per `claude_code.rs:49`) and a minimal 2-line `full.jsonl` (`system` + `user` with plain-string `message.content`).
- `test_index_with_checkpoint_branch` (462-491) and `test_index_reports_zero_without_checkpoint_branch` (447-460) exercise `dispatch_session` indirectly via the `ingest --json` CLI command, asserting `sessions_indexed` count and presence in `sessions --json --all`. Nothing asserts on `ingest_claude_code`'s witchcraft chunk output directly, nor on agent-name string values — these tests only need the current Claude-shaped fixture to keep parsing to 1 session; they don't lock in "Claude Code" as a literal string anywhere in assertions.
- No test uses "Codex" or exercises `dispatch_shadow_session`/`ingest_claude_code` output content directly.

## 4. `src/db.rs` schema

`sessions` table (db.rs:53-63): `agent_name TEXT NOT NULL` — free text, no CHECK/enum constraint, no per-agent index. No migrations reference agent type at all. Confirmed: safe to store any agent string.

## 5. Other hardcoded "Claude Code" / single-agent assumptions in `src/`

- `src/parsers/claude_code.rs:49,192` — `agent_name` defaults to `"Claude Code"` when metadata lacks the field (normal parse) and is hardcoded for shadow sessions (`parse_shadow_session`, line 192) — shadow-branch dispatch has **no way** to know the real agent since it only sees `full.jsonl`, no `metadata.json`.
- `src/parsers/mod.rs:19-26` — `dispatch_session`/`dispatch_shadow_session` unconditionally call `claude_code::parse_session`/`parse_shadow_session` regardless of the checkpoint's actual `agent` field (as already known).
- `src/commands/purge.rs:29` — comment-labeled section that purges `~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl` specifically (Claude-only cleanup path).
- `src/commands/init.rs:119,302,315,320,332` — registers/migrates only Claude Code hooks with entireio; no Codex equivalent.
- `src/ingest/claude_code.rs` — entire module (`ingest_claude_code`, `parse_session_content`, `Content`/`SessionInfo` structs) assumes Claude's `{"type":"user"/"assistant","message":{"content":...}}` shape; it's the sole populator of the witchcraft search DB, so Codex sessions currently get **no search indexing** at all (`src/commands/index.rs:338` only calls this one ingester).
- `src/commands/session_start.rs:31` — hardcoded `'Claude Code'` in SQL insert (hook is Claude-specific per `main.rs:123-126` comments, so an equivalent Codex hook/insert path doesn't exist yet).

## 1. `src/commands/show.rs` — transcript rendering

Fully hardcoded to Claude's JSONL shape. `parse()` (line 496) and its helpers `parse_user`/`parse_asst` (633-695) match on `v["type"] == "user"|"assistant"|"system"|"custom-title"` and read `v["message"]["content"]` as either a string or an array of `{"type":"text"|"tool_use"|"tool_result"}` blocks (539, 543, 636-663, 671-693). Tool names are resolved via a `tool_names` map built from `message.content[].type=="tool_use"` (497-510).

Given Codex's raw `full.jsonl` shape (`{"type":"response_item"|"event_msg"|..., "payload":{...}}`), every line would fail the `match v["type"].as_str()` arms (524-546, all `_ => {}`), so `parse()` would silently produce **zero cards** — `run_at` would print `"No messages found."` (145-148), not garbage, but effectively unusable for Codex sessions.

No reference to `transcript.jsonl`/`compact_transcript` anywhere in the file — only two unrelated comments mentioning "Claude Code transcript"/"local Claude transcript" (show.rs:444, 1420, 1458), referring to the local `~/.claude/projects/*.jsonl` file, not the checkpoint's `transcript.jsonl`.

## 2. `session_list.rs` / agent-aware logic

- `sanitize_one_line` (session_list.rs:73-89) collapses interior whitespace/newlines to a single space, purely a display-safety helper — not agent-specific.
- `augment_with_jsonls` (195-262) only scans `~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl` and hardcodes `agent_name: "Claude Code".to_string()` for any untracked session found there (line 254) — assumes every local JSONL is Claude.
- `src/commands/mod.rs:126-128`: `agent_color(_name: &str) -> u8 { 214 }` — the name parameter is **ignored**; every agent renders the same orange. No per-agent icon/branching logic exists anywhere else; `author_color` (134-144) is per-human, unrelated.
- `src/commands/sessions.rs:86` just passes through `s.agent_name` into JSON output, no branching.
- `src/entity/session.rs:5` — `agent_name: String` field, no enum.
- `src/commands/session_start.rs:31` hardcodes `'Claude Code'` literally into the `INSERT` SQL for the SessionStart-hook-created row.

## 3. `tests/integration_test.rs` fixtures

# Multi-agent session parsing: add a Codex/agnostic parser alongside Claude Code

## Context

Gossamer already has a `parsers` dispatch layer (`src/parsers/mod.rs`) whose `dispatch_session`/`dispatch_shadow_session` function names imply pluggable per-agent parsing, but only `parsers::claude_code` was ever implemented — every session, regardless of its actual agent, is parsed as if it were Claude Code's JSONL. Separately, `src/ingest/claude_code.rs` is the *only* populator of the semantic-search DB and is equally Claude-shape-specific.

Real data confirms the gap: `~/p/entire-graph`'s `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch has 72 checkpoints with `metadata.json.agent == "Codex"` alongside 61 `"Claude Code"` ones. Codex's raw `full.jsonl` has a structurally different, deeply-nested shape (`{"type":"response_item"|"event_msg", "payload": {...}}`) that the Claude-specific code silently fails to match — Codex sessions currently get no search indexing, and their session name/cwd/branch in the `sessions` table falls back to weak defaults.

Goal: parse Codex sessions too, using a **flexible/agnostic scraper** (per the user's direction) that extracts user/assistant turns and tool calls structurally — by recognizable field-name patterns — rather than a bespoke struct-per-format parser. Keep the existing Claude Code parser as the tuned, fast-path default; add the agnostic one as the fallback for everything else, so a third future agent format doesn't require another bespoke parser. Scope is the ingest/parsing layer only (DB `sessions` table + semantic search index) — the `show` transcript viewer stays Claude-only for now (explicitly confirmed with the user).

## Real-world shapes to design against

- **Checkpoint metadata.json** (`<x>/<id>/<num>/metadata.json`): both agents populate `agent` ("Claude Code" / "Codex") and the same `token_usage.output_tokens` shape — this part is already agent-agnostic and can be shared.
- **Claude `full.jsonl`**: lines shaped `{"type":"user"|"assistant"|"system"|"custom-title", "message":{"role":..,"content": string | [{"type":"text","text":..}, {"type":"tool_use",...}]}, "cwd":.., "gitBranch":.., "timestamp":..}`.
- **Codex raw `full.jsonl`** (used for both checkpoints and shadow branches — confirmed via `/00/a3e83616ee/0/full.jsonl` in entire-graph): top-level `{"type":"event_msg"|"response_item"|"session_meta"|"turn_context"|"world_state"|"compacted", "payload": {...}, "timestamp":..}`.
  - User text: `payload.type=="user_message"` → `payload.message`.
  - Assistant text: `payload.type=="agent_message"` → `payload.message`; `payload.type=="agent_reasoning"` → `payload.text` (short reasoning summary, worth keeping).
  - Tool calls: `payload.type in ("function_call","custom_tool_call")` → `payload.name` + `payload.arguments`/`payload.input`, correlated by `payload.call_id`.
  - Tool outputs: `payload.type in ("function_call_output","custom_tool_call_output")` → `payload.call_id` + `payload.output` (array of `{"text":..}`-ish blocks, but block `type` is `"input_text"`, not `"text"` — text extraction must key off the presence of a `.text` field, not its `type` tag).
  - Noise to skip: `reasoning` (encrypted), `session_meta`, `turn_context`, `world_state`, `compacted`, `token_count`, `task_started`/`task_complete`, `thread_settings_applied`, `message` blocks with `role in ("developer","system")`.
  - cwd is nested at `payload.cwd` on the `session_meta` line, not top-level.
- **Codex compact `transcript.jsonl`** (referenced by checkpoint metadata as `sessions[].compact_transcript`): pre-normalized, `{"type":"user"|"assistant","ts":..,"content":[{"text":..} | {"name":..,"input":..,"result":..}]}`. **Not reliable as the sole source** — confirmed empty (0 lines) for the Claude Code sample checked, and shadow branches don't have it at all. Treat it as just another shape the generic scraper happens to also handle, not a special-cased source file.

## Design: one agnostic scraper, reused by both consumers

New module **`src/scraper.rs`** (agent-agnostic, no git/DB knowledge), exposing:

```rust
pub enum Role { User, Assistant }
pub struct Turn { pub role: Role, pub text: String, pub timestamp: Option<String>, pub ts_ms: i64 }
pub struct ScanInfo { pub cwd: Option<String>, pub branch: Option<String> }

pub fn looks_like_claude_shape(jsonl_bytes: &[u8]) -> bool;   // sniff for shadow-branch dispatch
pub fn scan(jsonl_bytes: &[u8]) -> (ScanInfo, Vec<Turn>);     // the agnostic walker
```

`scan()` processes each line as a `serde_json::Value` and applies structural, name-based signal matching (not per-agent branches):

1. **Role classification** — checks, on the line itself and on `line["payload"]` (Codex raw's one level of nesting): a `role` field (`"user"`/`"assistant"`, skip `"developer"`/`"system"`), or a `type`/`payload.type` in a small synonym table (`"user"→User`, `"user_message"→User`, `"assistant"→Assistant`, `"agent_message"→Assistant`, `"agent_reasoning"→Assistant`).
2. **Text extraction** — a small recursive helper harvests string values from known text-bearing key names (`text`, `message`) wherever they appear on the classified envelope, plus walks `content`/`output`/`result` arrays: for array blocks, treat any block with a `.text` string as text regardless of its declared `type`; treat a block/object with `.name` + (`.input` or `.arguments`) as a tool call → format `"[Tool: {name}] {truncated args}"`.
3. **Tool call/result correlation** — maintain a `HashMap<call_id, turn_index>` while scanning; when a `function_call`/`custom_tool_call` line is seen, push a new Assistant turn and record its index by `call_id`; when the matching `*_output` line arrives, append its extracted text to that turn (`"\n→ {output}"`). Compact-transcript's inline `result` field (same block, no separate line) is handled by the same block-level extraction in step 2 — no correlation needed there.
4. **Session-level info** — `cwd`/`branch`/`gitBranch` collected the same way (top-level or one level under `payload`), first non-empty value wins.
5. Everything unmatched is skipped (this is where `session_meta`, `turn_context`, `world_state`, `token_count`, `reasoning`, `task_started/complete` naturally fall through).

`looks_like_claude_shape` sniffs the first few parseable lines for the unambiguous Claude signature (top-level `type` in the Claude enum *and* a `message.role`/`message.content`) — used only where there's no `metadata.json` to consult (shadow branches).

This single scraper is consumed by two thin, format-specific-but-agent-agnostic layers:

### `src/parsers/generic.rs`
Mirrors `parsers/claude_code.rs`'s public shape (`parse_session`, `parse_shadow_session` → `ParsedSession`), but built on `scraper::scan`:
- `parse_session(meta_bytes, jsonl_bytes)`: parse `metadata.json` for `session_id`/`agent`/`created_at`/`branch`/`token_usage` (reuse/share the `SessionMetadata` deserialize struct currently private to `claude_code.rs` — hoist it to `parsers/mod.rs` since the shape is identical for both agents). Run `scraper::scan` on the jsonl for `cwd`, `branch` override, and turns; derive `session_name` from the first meaningful `User` turn (reuse `claude_code::is_wrapper_prompt`, made `pub(crate)`) and `updated_at` from the max turn timestamp.
- `parse_shadow_session(jsonl_bytes, session_id)`: same, but no metadata — derive `agent_name` best-effort from any `payload.originator` string seen on a `session_meta`-shaped line (e.g. `"Codex Desktop"` → `"Codex"`), falling back to `"Unknown Agent"`.

Update `parsers/mod.rs`:
- `dispatch_session`: parse just the `agent` field out of `meta_bytes` first; if it case-insensitively contains `"claude"` (or is absent — preserves current default), use `claude_code::parse_session`, else `generic::parse_session`.
- `dispatch_shadow_session`: no metadata available, so use `scraper::looks_like_claude_shape(jsonl_bytes)` to pick `claude_code::parse_shadow_session` vs `generic::parse_shadow_session`.

### `src/ingest/generic.rs`
Mirrors `ingest/claude_code.rs`'s per-session chunking (`ingest_session(db, session_id, content, project_name) -> Result<(usize, Option<String>)>`), built on `scraper::scan` instead of the Claude-specific `parse_session_content`. Groups `Turn`s into interactions the same way (split on `User` turns), reuses `claude_code::sanitize`/`MIN_CHUNK_CODEPOINTS`/`MAX_CHUNK_CODEPOINTS` (made `pub(crate)`) for text cleanup and length filtering, and writes docs with `"source": <agent_name lowercased>` (e.g. `"codex"`) — confirmed safe: `commands/search.rs::parse_hit` only special-cases `"session"`/`"repo"`/`"checkpoint"`, everything else (including today's `"claude"`) falls through the same generic transcript-hit branch, so `"codex"` needs no changes there. Uses a distinct UUIDv5 namespace constant (mirrors `CLAUDE_CODE_NAMESPACE`) so doc IDs don't collide.

### Ingest driver refactor (`ingest/mod.rs` + `ingest/claude_code.rs`)
Currently `ingest_claude_code()` in `claude_code.rs` *is* the repo-walking driver (fetches watermark, walks meta paths, dedups checkpoints, indexes commit messages, sweeps shadow branches) and hardcodes a call to its own `ingest_session`. Move that driver logic (the git/DB parts: `ingest_repo`, `index_checkpoint_commits`, watermark handling) into `ingest/mod.rs` as a new agent-agnostic `pub fn ingest_checkpoint_sessions(db: &mut DB) -> Result<usize>`, mirroring the dispatch pattern already established in `parsers/mod.rs`. Inside the per-session loop, read `meta["agent"]` (already deserializing `meta` there) and dispatch to `claude_code::ingest_session` or `generic::ingest_session` accordingly. Leave `claude_code.rs` holding only the Claude-specific `ingest_session`/`parse_session_content`/`sanitize`/etc. (pure format parsing, no git/DB code) — same separation of concerns the `parsers` module already has.
Update the 3 call sites (`commands/index.rs:338`, `commands/attach.rs:29`, `commands/session_stop.rs:27`) from `ingest::claude_code::ingest_claude_code(...)` to `ingest::ingest_checkpoint_sessions(...)`.

### Shadow-branch generic name inference
`ParsedSession.agent_name` from `parsers::generic::parse_shadow_session` is best-effort (no metadata.json exists for shadow branches). Document this as a known limitation rather than trying to guess perfectly.

## Files touched

- **New:** `src/scraper.rs`, `src/parsers/generic.rs`, `src/ingest/generic.rs`
- **Edited:** `src/main.rs` (add `mod scraper;`), `src/parsers/mod.rs` (dispatch + hoist shared metadata struct), `src/parsers/claude_code.rs` (expose `is_wrapper_prompt` as `pub(crate)`, no behavior change), `src/ingest/mod.rs` (new `ingest_checkpoint_sessions` driver), `src/ingest/claude_code.rs` (trim to pure parser, expose `sanitize`/constants as `pub(crate)`), `src/commands/index.rs`, `src/commands/attach.rs`, `src/commands/session_stop.rs` (call-site rename)
- **Docs:** update `AGENTS.md`'s description of the `ingest` pipeline (function name change, mention of the generic parser) to keep it accurate, since it's checked-in documentation the user relies on.

## Verification

1. `cargo build --release` compiles clean.
2. `cargo test --test integration_test` — existing Claude-shaped fixtures must keep passing unchanged (confirmed no test currently asserts on the `ingest_claude_code` name or literal "Claude Code" string, only on session counts).
3. Manual smoke test against real data: point a scratch clone of `~/p/entire-graph` (or run directly against it if the user's OK with read-only `entire gossamer ingest --json` there) and confirm `sessions_indexed`/`log_turns` counts increase to cover the 72 Codex checkpoints, and `entire gossamer search <term-known-to-appear-in-a-codex-session> --json` returns hits with `"source":"codex"`-tagged bodies containing recognizable `[Tool: ...]` lines.
4. Spot-check a couple of Codex `full.jsonl` fixtures fetched into the scratchpad dir (not `/tmp`) as unit-test input for `scraper::scan`, asserting expected `Turn` counts/roles/text for known lines (user_message, agent_message, function_call+output correlation).

# Multi-agent session parsing: add a Codex/agnostic parser alongside Claude Code

## Context

Gossamer already has a `parsers` dispatch layer (`src/parsers/mod.rs`) whose `dispatch_session`/`dispatch_shadow_session` function names imply pluggable per-agent parsing, but only `parsers::claude_code` was ever implemented — every session, regardless of its actual agent, is parsed as if it were Claude Code's JSONL. Separately, `src/ingest/claude_code.rs` is the *only* populator of the semantic-search DB and is equally Claude-shape-specific.

Real data confirms the gap: `~/p/entire-graph`'s `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch has 72 checkpoints with `metadata.json.agent == "Codex"` alongside 61 `"Claude Code"` ones. Codex's raw `full.jsonl` has a structurally different, deeply-nested shape (`{"type":"response_item"|"event_msg", "payload": {...}}`) that the Claude-specific code silently fails to match — Codex sessions currently get no search indexing, and their session name/cwd/branch in the `sessions` table falls back to weak defaults.

Goal: parse Codex sessions too, using a **flexible/agnostic scraper** (per the user's direction) that extracts user/assistant turns and tool calls structurally — by recognizable field-name patterns — rather than a bespoke struct-per-format parser. Keep the existing Claude Code parser as the tuned, fast-path default; add the agnostic one as the fallback for everything else, so a third future agent format doesn't require another bespoke parser. Scope is the ingest/parsing layer only (DB `sessions` table + semantic search index) — the `show` transcript viewer stays Claude-only for now (explicitly confirmed with the user).

## Real-world shapes to design against

- **Checkpoint metadata.json** (`<x>/<id>/<num>/metadata.json`): both agents populate `agent` ("Claude Code" / "Codex") and the same `token_usage.output_tokens` shape — this part is already agent-agnostic and can be shared.
- **Claude `full.jsonl`**: lines shaped `{"type":"user"|"assistant"|"system"|"custom-title", "message":{"role":..,"content": string | [{"type":"text","text":..}, {"type":"tool_use",...}]}, "cwd":.., "gitBranch":.., "timestamp":..}`.
- **Codex raw `full.jsonl`** (used for both checkpoints and shadow branches — confirmed via `/00/a3e83616ee/0/full.jsonl` in entire-graph): top-level `{"type":"event_msg"|"response_item"|"session_meta"|"turn_context"|"world_state"|"compacted", "payload": {...}, "timestamp":..}`.
  - User text: `payload.type=="user_message"` → `payload.message`.
  - Assistant text: `payload.type=="agent_message"` → `payload.message`; `payload.type=="agent_reasoning"` → `payload.text` (short reasoning summary, worth keeping).
  - Tool calls: `payload.type in ("function_call","custom_tool_call")` → `payload.name` + `payload.arguments`/`payload.input`, correlated by `payload.call_id`.
  - Tool outputs: `payload.type in ("function_call_output","custom_tool_call_output")` → `payload.call_id` + `payload.output` (array of `{"text":..}`-ish blocks, but block `type` is `"input_text"`, not `"text"` — text extraction must key off the presence of a `.text` field, not its `type` tag).
  - Noise to skip: `reasoning` (encrypted), `session_meta`, `turn_context`, `world_state`, `compacted`, `token_count`, `task_started`/`task_complete`, `thread_settings_applied`, `message` blocks with `role in ("developer","system")`.
  - cwd is nested at `payload.cwd` on the `session_meta` line, not top-level.
- **Codex compact `transcript.jsonl`** (referenced by checkpoint metadata as `sessions[].compact_transcript`): pre-normalized, `{"type":"user"|"assistant","ts":..,"content":[{"text":..} | {"name":..,"input":..,"result":..}]}`. **Not reliable as the sole source** — confirmed empty (0 lines) for the Claude Code sample checked, and shadow branches don't have it at all. Treat it as just another shape the generic scraper happens to also handle, not a special-cased source file.

## Design: one agnostic scraper, reused by both consumers

New module **`src/scraper.rs`** (agent-agnostic, no git/DB knowledge), exposing:

```rust
pub enum Role { User, Assistant }
pub struct Turn { pub role: Role, pub text: String, pub timestamp: Option<String>, pub ts_ms: i64 }
pub struct ScanInfo { pub cwd: Option<String>, pub branch: Option<String> }

pub fn looks_like_claude_shape(jsonl_bytes: &[u8]) -> bool;   // sniff for shadow-branch dispatch
pub fn scan(jsonl_bytes: &[u8]) -> (ScanInfo, Vec<Turn>);     // the agnostic walker
```

`scan()` processes each line as a `serde_json::Value` and applies structural, name-based signal matching (not per-agent branches):

1. **Role classification** — checks, on the line itself and on `line["payload"]` (Codex raw's one level of nesting): a `role` field (`"user"`/`"assistant"`, skip `"developer"`/`"system"`), or a `type`/`payload.type` in a small synonym table (`"user"→User`, `"user_message"→User`, `"assistant"→Assistant`, `"agent_message"→Assistant`, `"agent_reasoning"→Assistant`).
2. **Text extraction** — a small recursive helper harvests string values from known text-bearing key names (`text`, `message`) wherever they appear on the classified envelope, plus walks `content`/`output`/`result` arrays: for array blocks, treat any block with a `.text` string as text regardless of its declared `type`; treat a block/object with `.name` + (`.input` or `.arguments`) as a tool call → format `"[Tool: {name}] {truncated args}"`.
3. **Tool call/result correlation** — maintain a `HashMap<call_id, turn_index>` while scanning; when a `function_call`/`custom_tool_call` line is seen, push a new Assistant turn and record its index by `call_id`; when the matching `*_output` line arrives, append its extracted text to that turn (`"\n→ {output}"`). 4. **Session-level info** — `cwd`/`branch`/`gitBranch` collected the same way (top-level or one level under `payload`), first non-empty value wins.

# AGENTS.md — Gossamer

## What is Gossamer?

Gossamer is an **Entire CLI plugin** that tracks AI coding sessions across git repositories. It ships as the binary `entire-gossamer` and is invoked as `entire gossamer ...` (or directly as `entire-gossamer ...` once installed — see [entire-plugin.yml](entire-plugin.yml)). It sits on top of **entireio** (`entire`), a session checkpointing tool that commits AI agent conversation logs to a dedicated git branch (`entire/checkpoints/v1`). Gossamer adds:

- A SQLite database (`~/.gossamer/gossamer.db`) that indexes sessions and repositories
- An interactive TUI (terminal UI) for browsing repos and sessions
- Semantic search over session transcripts via **witchcraft** (a local embedding/vector-search library)
- Shell integration (`gr` function for `cd`-ing into a tracked repo)
- Claude Code hook integration (auto-ingests sessions on start/stop)
- Git worktree management (`entire` has no concept of worktrees) and a locally browsable transcript view (`entire` only exposes raw transcript bytes, not a normalized structure)

## Plugin Mechanism

Entire CLI plugins are discovered as `entire-<name>` executables on `$PATH` or in Entire's managed plugin directory (`~/.local/share/entire/plugins/bin` by default). `entire-plugin.yml` at the repo root (`name: gossamer`) is metadata only — the actual dispatch is `entire gossamer <args...>` → `entire-gossamer <args...>` (argv passthrough, no RPC). Install/update with:

```bash
cargo build --release
entire plugin install ./target/release/entire-gossamer --force
```

## Repository Layout

```
src/
  main.rs              # CLI entry point, Clap command definitions
  db.rs                # SQLite connection + schema migrations
  config.rs            # Witchcraft assets path config (~/.gossamer/warp_assets)
  watermark.rs         # File mtime utilities
  entity/
    repository.rs      # Repository struct
    session.rs         # Session struct
  commands/
    init.rs            # `entire gossamer init` — repo registration, hook installation
    status.rs          # `entire gossamer repo` — TUI repo browser + launch wizard
    sessions.rs        # `entire gossamer sessions` — TUI session list
    show.rs            # `entire gossamer show` — session transcript viewer
    search.rs          # `entire gossamer search` — semantic search TUI
    index.rs           # `entire gossamer ingest` — full ingest from checkpoint branch

40	    index.rs           # `entire gossamer ingest` — full ingest from checkpoint branch
41	    refresh.rs         # `entire gossamer ingest --incremental` — incremental ingest (new commits only)
42	    new_session.rs     # `entire gossamer launch` — launch agent in optional worktree
43	    resume.rs          # `entire gossamer resume` — resume a session (worktree-aware)
44	    clean.rs           # `entire gossamer clean` — delete session from DB + search index
45	    attach.rs          # `entire gossamer attach` — attach an existing entire session
46	    session_start.rs   # `entire gossamer session-start` — Claude Code SessionStart hook
47	    session_stop.rs    # `entire gossamer session-stop` — Claude Code Stop hook
48	  ingest/
49	    mod.rs             # Search DB ingestion: sessions, repos, embed + index
50	    claude_code.rs     # Ingest Claude Code session logs from checkpoint branch
51	tests/
52	  integration_test.rs  # Integration tests (binary invocation, isolated HOME)
53	```
54	
55	## Commands
56	
57	All commands that produce output have a `--json` flag that switches from interactive TUI to machine-readable JSON on stdout.
58	
59	### `entire gossamer init`
60	
61	Registers the current git repository with gossamer. Steps:
62	
63	1. Reads `git remote get-url origin` for the remote URL and derives the repo name from it.
64	2. Checks for `.entire/settings.json` or the `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch. If neither exists, runs an interactive wizard that calls `entire configure` and `entire agent add <agent>`.
65	3. Installs a post-commit hook (`.git/hooks/post-commit`) that runs `entire gossamer ingest` after checkpoint commits.
66	4. Installs Claude Code hooks (`~/.claude/settings.json`): `SessionStart` → `entire gossamer session-start`, `Stop` → `entire gossamer session-stop`. If an existing hook still points at the pre-rename `gossamer session-start`/`gossamer session-stop` commands, it's migrated to `entire gossamer ...` in place rather than duplicated (see `upsert_hook_command` in `init.rs`). Hook/shell-integration commands go through `entire gossamer ...` rather than calling the `entire-gossamer` binary by name directly, because Entire's managed plugin directory is only on `$PATH` inside `entire`'s own subprocess dispatch — not necessarily in the shell a git hook or Claude Code hook runs in.
67	5. Installs a `gr` shell function in `~/.zshrc` or `~/.bash_profile` for interactive `cd`.
68	6. Inserts the repo into the `repositories` table.
69	
70	**Requires:** a git repo with an `origin` remote. Safe to run multiple times (idempotent).
71	
72	### `entire gossamer repo` (default command)
73	
74	Interactive TUI listing all tracked repositories. From the repo list you can:
75	- `space` / `→` — drill into a repo's sessions and worktrees
76	- `s` — open the launch wizard (agent picker → optional branch → name → prompt)
77	- `c` — `cd` to the repo (only when invoked via the `gr` shell wrapper)
78	- `/` — semantic search
79	
80	From the sessions sub-screen:
81	- `space` / `→` — view session transcript (`entire gossamer show`)
82	- `r` — resume session
83	- `n` — create a new git worktree
84	- `s` — launch wizard
85	
86	`--json` output: `{ "repos": [ { "name", "directory", "remote", "worktrees": [...], "sessions": [...] } ] }`
87	
88	### `entire gossamer sessions [--all]`
89	
90	Lists sessions from the past 3 days (or all with `--all`). Sources:
91	1. The `sessions` table in the gossamer DB (sessions ingested from checkpoint branch).
92	2. JSONL files in `~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl` (live Claude Code sessions not yet ingested).
93	
94	Sessions from the current repo are shown first, then by recency. Interactive TUI with same keybindings as above.
95	
96	`--json` output: `{ "sessions": [ { "session_id", "session_name", "cwd", "branch", "agent", "updated_at", "backed_up" } ] }`
97	
98	### `entire gossamer ingest [--json] [--incremental]`
99	
100	Ingests all tracked repos' `entire/checkpoints/v1` branches into the local DB — the layer that gives gossamer a locally browsable view of checkpoints (entire itself only exposes raw transcript bytes via `entire session info --transcript`, not a normalized structure).
101	
102	Without `--incremental`, does a full re-ingest. For each repo:
103	1. Optionally fetches the branch from a remote checkpoint URL (from `.entire/settings.json`).
104	2. Runs `git ls-tree -r --name-only entire/checkpoints/v1` to find `metadata.json` files at paths matching `<x>/<session_id>/<number>/metadata.json`.
105	3. Parses each session's metadata and JSONL transcript, upserts into the `sessions` table.
106	4. Ingests session names, repo info, and Claude Code logs into the witchcraft search DB.
107	5. Embeds and indexes if witchcraft assets are configured.
108	
109	`--json` output: `{ "sessions_indexed", "log_turns", "session_names", "repos" }`

Hook/shell-integration commands go through `entire gossamer ...` rather than calling the `entire-gossamer` binary by name directly, because Entire's managed plugin directory is only on `$PATH` inside `entire`'s own subprocess dispatch — not necessarily in the shell a git hook or Claude Code hook runs in.
5. Installs a `gr` shell function in `~/.zshrc` or `~/.bash_profile` for interactive `cd`.

### `entire gossamer sessions [--all]`

Lists sessions from the past 3 days (or all with `--all`). Sources:
1. The `sessions` table in the gossamer DB (sessions ingested from checkpoint branch).
2. JSONL files in `~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl` (live Claude Code sessions not yet ingested).

Sessions from the current repo are shown first, then by recency. Interactive TUI with same keybindings as above.

`--json` output: `{ "sessions": [ { "session_id", "session_name", "cwd", "branch", "agent", "updated_at", "backed_up" } ] }`

### `entire gossamer ingest [--json] [--incremental]`

Ingests all tracked repos' `entire/checkpoints/v1` branches into the local DB — the layer that gives gossamer a locally browsable view of checkpoints (entire itself only exposes raw transcript bytes via `entire session info --transcript`, not a normalized structure).

Without `--incremental`, does a full re-ingest. For each repo:

content.text:
I've applied two additional fixes discovered from real-data verification and am waiting on a fresh ingest run to confirm them.

**Additional fixes since last update:**
1. **Duplicate turns** — Codex's raw log emits the same user/assistant message twice (once as an `event_msg` UI notification, once as the `response_item` conversation-history entry). Added consecutive-duplicate collapsing in `scraper::scan`, verified against the real fixture (turn count dropped from 9664 → 8765, confirming ~900 real duplicates removed).
2. **Session naming** — reusing Claude's `is_wrapper_prompt` (which only recognizes Claude's own tag names like `<command-message>`) caused Codex session names to pick up its own wrapper tags (`<environment_context>`, `<recommended_plugins>`) as if they were real user intent. Replaced with a genuinely tag-name-agnostic check in `scraper.rs` (matches the *shape* of an opening XML-ish tag, not a specific list) — now correctly recognized for both agents.

Both are covered by new unit tests; all 6 scraper tests and the full integration suite (minus the one pre-existing, unrelated failure) pass. Waiting on a real `entire gossamer ingest` run against your tracked repos to do final end-to-end confirmation.

content.text:
All work is complete, built, tested, and installed. Here's the summary:

**What changed:**
- **`src/scraper.rs`** (new) — agent-agnostic transcript walker. Classifies user/assistant turns by structural signal (a `role` field, or `type` synonyms like `user_message`/`agent_message`), extracts text from `text`/`message`/`content` keys regardless of nesting depth, formats tool calls as `[Tool: name] args → output` with call-ID correlation across separate call/output lines, and collapses Codex's real duplicate-envelope logging. 7 unit tests, all passing.
- **`src/parsers/generic.rs`** + **`src/ingest/generic.rs`** (new) — Codex/agnostic parsers for the `sessions` table and the semantic-search index, built on the scraper. Claude Code keeps its existing bespoke parsers untouched; dispatch happens by `metadata.json`'s `agent` field (or JSONL-shape sniffing for shadow branches).
- Refactored the ingest driver (`ingest_claude_code` → `ingest::ingest_checkpoint_sessions`) so it dispatches per-session like the `parsers` module already did, rather than being hardwired to Claude.
- Fixed a pre-existing crash (`session_id[..8]` panic on short IDs) that was blocking `entire gossamer ingest` entirely on your `~/cli` repo's test-fixture checkpoints — confirmed present on unmodified `main`, unrelated to this feature, but blocking verification.
- Updated `AGENTS.md` to document the new layout.

**Verified against your real `~/p/entire-graph` data:**
- The `sessions` table now correctly shows all 7 Codex sessions with real, meaningful names (e.g. "Continue the Entire Graph/V7 work...", "Review all open PRs for the entire-graph project") — confirmed live in your `~/.gossamer/gossamer.db`.
- Search-index chunking verified via isolated tests against the actual 28k-line Codex transcript: tool calls, arguments, and outputs all render correctly and are labeled `[User]`/`[Codex]` like Claude's chunks.

**One known caveat:** the full `entire gossamer ingest` run against your production DB hit a transient `database is locked` error from witchcraft's search-DB write step (WAL file was 194MB, so it's genuinely under heavy write load from `~/cli`'s large backlog of test-fixture checkpoints). This looks environmental, not something my changes introduced — the DB-metadata layer completed successfully before it, and I verified the search-chunking logic works correctly in isolation. You may want to just retry `entire gossamer ingest` when things are quieter, or investigate a busy-timeout setting in witchcraft separately.

+/// Render a tool call's `input` back to a compact display string. Our own
+/// single-field synthetic wrapper (`{"input": "<raw string>"}`, used when the

content.text:
**Done — the transcript viewer now renders Codex sessions properly.**

What I built:
- Refactored `scraper.rs`'s `Turn` type to carry structured `Part`s (`Text` / `ToolCall { id, name, input, result }`, uncapped) instead of pre-flattened strings, plus a `turn_text()` helper that flattens for the search-index use case. This is what let `show.rs` render tool calls as real interactive elements rather than plain text blobs.
- `show.rs`'s `parse()` now dispatches by agent (same pattern as `parsers`/`ingest`): Claude Code keeps its existing per-line JSONL walker unchanged; every other agent goes through a new `parse_generic_lines()` built on `scraper::scan`. Both produce the same `Card` list and run through the **same** existing post-processing pipeline (merge consecutive assistant turns → split into text + `ToolRound` cards), so tool-call rendering, navigation, and the XML-wrapper-tag collapsing (`<environment_context>` etc.) all work identically for both agents with no changes to the renderer itself.
- Added 4 new tests (2 in `scraper.rs` for structured tool-call parsing, 2 in `show.rs` for the dispatch) — all pass, plus verified against a real Codex session from `~/p/entire-graph`: 152 cards generated correctly (61 user, 53 assistant, 37 grouped tool-call rounds, correct header cwd/agent).

Full test suite passes (aside from the same pre-existing unrelated failure), release build reinstalled. Try `entire gossamer show 019f6148-2b1a-7522-adec-081e066879a4` (or any Codex session) to see it live.

Same pre-existing unrelated failure, everything else passes. Reinstalled.

**What changed:** in the `show` transcript viewer, Up/Down arrow keys now scroll the viewport one line at a time, completely decoupled from message selection — so a message taller than the screen can finally be read all the way through instead of the view snapping back to its top every frame. `j`/`k` still jump between whole messages (and pull the newly-selected one into view, as before). `u`/PageUp/PageDown now do a genuine half-screen scroll instead of being immediately undone by the old per-frame re-snap. Updated the footer hint (`j/k next/prev  ↑↓ scroll`) to match, and added 6 unit tests locking in the new scroll-snapping behavior.
